title: Understanding Mixtures and Their Separation Techniques

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how to separate sand from water after playing at the beach? Let's explore how mixtures work and how we can separate them.

blocks.markdown: A mixture is a combination of two or more substances where each substance retains its own chemical identity. Unlike pure substances, mixtures can be separated into their individual components by physical methods.

blocks.title: Definition of a Mixture
blocks.text: A mixture is a physical combination of two or more substances that are not chemically combined.

blocks.markdown: Common methods to separate mixtures include filtration, evaporation, and decantation. Each method is suitable for different types of mixtures.

blocks.title: Separating Sand and Water
blocks.prompt: How can you separate sand from a mixture of sand and water?

steps.text: Pour the mixture through a filter paper placed in a funnel.
The sand will remain on the filter paper, while the water will pass through.

blocks.answer: Filtration is used to separate sand from water.

blocks.markdown: Filtration involves passing a mixture through a filter, which allows the liquid to pass through while retaining the solid particles. Evaporation is used to separate a dissolved solid from a liquid by heating the mixture until the liquid evaporates. Decantation involves carefully pouring off a liquid to leave the solid behind.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember that the choice of separation method depends on the physical properties of the components in the mixture.

points: Mixtures consist of two or more substances that can be separated by physical means.
Filtration, evaporation, and decantation are common methods for separating mixtures.
